deterministicTests.environment: simulated (fake host); every scenario checks the state transitions AND the input that reached or did not reach each window

linux.name: M3.2 A: an ACTIVE window closes -> TARGET_LOST, scheduler registration revoked, no input afterwards, the other table plays on
M3.2 B: a GAMEPLAY-PAUSED window closes -> the health monitor detects it (the operator T5 failure), registration revoked, nothing resumes
M3.2 C: an action the table did not apply (rejected, no change) -> SAFETY_PAUSED input-rejected; then the window closes -> TARGET_LOST
M3.2 D: an UNCONFIRMED (timed-out) input, then the window closes -> the uncertain input stays recorded for review and TARGET_LOST is reached
M3.2 E: the window closes DURING an identity probe -> the stale "healthy" answer authorises nothing; a late answer after the loss is discarded
M3.2 F: the handle is reused by ANOTHER process while paused -> identity-changed TARGET_LOST; the old registration can never be used again
M3.2 G: table 2 is lost while TABLE 1 holds the cursor lease -> table 1 is not cancelled and completes its action
M3.2 H: table 2 is lost while ITS OWN input is queued -> the queued action is rejected (target-lost), table 1 continues
M3.2 I: table 2 is lost while IT holds the cursor lease -> its input is cancelled before the press; table 1 is isolated
M3.2 J: emergency stop and target loss together -> TARGET_LOST wins for the closed table; nothing restarts automatically after the reset
M3.2 K: a paused window that stays open is monitored, its lifecycle stays accurate, and nothing resumes gameplay
M3.2 L: a completed tournament stays stopped: monitoring continues but never restarts it; a later close is still recognised
M3.2 M: re-registration needs a fresh authorisation and identity; the lost registration stays refused
M3.2 N: a confirmation that arrives late, after the attempt was cancelled, causes no retry and no second action
M3.2 O: a valid fresh action is confirmed: input status confirmed, timings recorded, no evidence record
M3.2 P: a real "simulator rejected the action" outcome -> input-rejected safety pause, complete evidence, no retry, operator resume recovers
M3.2 Q: two tables under repeated faults (unapplied actions, pauses, closes and replacements) -> never any cross-table input
M3.2 R: several table windows close and are re-registered one after another -> each loss isolated, each replacement plays

linuxUnits.name: M3.2 unit: the health monitor never moves a lifecycle towards ACTIVE and never resumes anything
M3.2 unit: unknown answers prove nothing and back off; a loss is reported exactly once (single-flight) and the monitor stops
M3.2 unit: probes made by the table count as evidence (no duplicate probe while playing); a paused table is due on the short interval
M3.2 unit: scheduler registrations - revoke once, refuse the old registration for good, a replacement is available, an old pause never blocks it
M3.2 unit: invalidating one registration never touches another table's queued or running job

scenarios.name: Scripted practice plays hand after hand (no regression)
Simulator restarts with a different handle
Temporary capture failures (injected while the window stays open)
Identity mismatch / handle reuse: no inherited permission
Window resized while playing (geometry / display-scaling re-check)
Hands that start with eliminated players are tracked (the Milestone 2 stall)
A tournament is played to its end; the end is a normal stop
A hand first seen after its opening: untracked, no input; recovery at the next verified hand
Think-time holds: one seat acting on consecutive streets with every control hidden (pre-existing defect fixed in M3)
Two tables: eliminations on both, one window closes; no input crosses tables
Two tables: table 2 paused by an action its table did not apply, then its window closes (the operator failure, reproduced)
Emergency stop right after an elimination: stop wins, no input, no automatic recovery
